subject: RowHouse Bank — Support engagement deep dive: TAM coverage & incident comms
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@rowhousebank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@rowhousebank.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Support model & TAM coverage — follow-ups

Ben — thanks again for the demo yesterday. RowHouse is compiling the RFI appendix that covers operational support and incident communications. Two quick asks to kick off: 1) can you provide a single-sheet matrix that maps TAM coverage hours, on-call handoffs, and expected response / remediation SLAs by severity for Dedicated deployments? 2) we need a short summary of how you handle audit evidence requests (SOC2 logs, API request traces) and typical lead times for access.

Also looping Mike (infrastructure) — he may have narrower questions about log retention windows. Happy to take an outline first; we can refine into the form we'll include with the procurement packet.

Laura Chen
Head of Cloud Ops
RowHouse Bank

Attachments: none

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@rowhousebank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@rowhousebank.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Support model & TAM coverage — follow-ups

Laura — thanks for the note and great meeting yesterday. I've attached a compact support matrix (RowHouse_RFI_support_matrix.xlsx) that maps our TAM coverage windows, on-call rotation, first-response vs. target remediation for Severity 1–4, and the escalation ladder for Dedicated and Private deployments. High level:

- TAM coverage: US business hours dedicated TAM + 24/7 on-call escalation for Sev1 for Dedicated customers with an SLA addendum (we can make the hours explicit in the SOW).
- Handoffs: we support daily on-call handover notes (template included) and a weekly sync for higher-touch customers.
- Evidence & audits: we provide SOC2 summary and can deliver API request traces and audit logs via a secure share; typical lead time for self-service data exports is 48 hours, formal evidence packages often delivered within 5 business days depending on scope.

Couple of clarifying Qs so we tailor the package properly:
1) For Sev1, do you require dedicated engineer phone escalation (pager) or is Slack/IMS sufficient as the primary alerting channel?
2) Are you expecting data retention beyond our standard 90-day request-trace window for the RFP? If yes, what retention duration?

I'll follow up with a short runbook extract inline and the matrix attached.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: RowHouse_RFI_support_matrix.xlsx

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@rowhousebank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@rowhousebank.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Support model & TAM coverage — follow-ups

Ben — this is terrific, thanks for the quick turn. A few follow-ups after reviewing the matrix:

- For Sev1 we do want a phone/pager escalation path in addition to Slack. The vendor must be able to provide immediate voice contact for 24/7 Sev1 incidents.
- Regarding retention: for regulatory purposes we need 12 months of request-trace logs for a selected subset of accounts; full 12-month export is preferred but if there are constraints, we can define a scoped export (e.g., payment pipelines only). Please note this may go into the procurement SOW as a retention exhibit.
- Can you confirm whether your on-call rotation enforces maximum continuous on-call duration (e.g., no one on-call for more than X consecutive days) and whether you provide a documented handoff template?

Also attaching our internal audit intake template so you can see the evidence doc format we prefer (we may submit as part of the formal request).

Laura Chen
Head of Cloud Ops
RowHouse Bank

Attachments: RowHouse_audit_intake_template.docx

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@rowhousebank.com>, Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@rowhousebank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Support model & TAM coverage — follow-ups

Laura — thanks for the details and the intake template. Quick answers and next steps so procurement has what it needs:

1) Phone escalation: confirmed. For Dedicated + Private we can add a 24/7 voice escalation contact in the SOW (primary TAM + on-call escalation engineer). We'll include a contact rotation with a pager/phone number for Sev1 incidents.

2) Retention: RowHouse's request for 12-month request-trace retention is possible as a scoped export. Our standard platform retention for request traces is 90 days; to meet 12 months we offer two options: a) scheduled archival exports to your secure S3 (monthly snapshots) included as a procurement exhibit, or b) extended retention on our side under a separate retention addendum (costed). We'll include both options and an example cost delta in the RFP appendix.

3) On-call limits & handoffs: we enforce a maximum of 7 consecutive days per on-call engineer and rotate teams across regions for longer windows. We do provide a documented handoff template (see the included runbook excerpt in the matrix). Handoff notes capture incident state, mitigations in-flight, next steps, and contact points.

Next steps:
- Ben will provide a short excerpt of the on-call handoff template inline to include in your packet.
- Karthik will draft an evidence access checklist (SOC2 summary + trace export process) and confirm expected delivery SLA for formal auditor requests.
- We'll update the support matrix to show the two retention options and include a sample SOW line item for 24/7 voice escalation.

If that works, can we aim to deliver the updated appendix by COB Mon 23 Jun?

Thanks — Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0221

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf
